row.evidence: Help Scout's SSO docs say "Service Provider (Help Scout) provisioning is not supported. Accounts should be created first in the IdP or Help Scout"; no SCIM is offered on any plan.
row.notes: No SCIM at any tier; SAML SSO only. SSO/SAML is included on Pro ($75/user/mo annual, minimum 10 users) and sold as an add-on on Standard and Plus (add-on price not listed); the SSO help article disagrees (see conflicts). Users can be created, listed and deleted through the Inbox API (Standard and up, 200/400/800 calls per minute by plan), and Google Workspace users can be imported through the Marketplace app. Confidence lowered from high to medium: no Help Scout page says SCIM is not offered (the 'provisioning is not supported' note is about SAML sign-in), so none rests on absence after checking the pricing page, the docs search and sitemap, and the API reference. The SWA-only Okta app maps to idp.okta none.

limitations.text: Help Scout does not support service-provider provisioning; accounts must exist before SAML sign-in.

endpoints.purpose: List users (including those who have not accepted invites)
Create a user (admin, user or light user role; optional invite email)

rate_limits.text: Per account, by plan: Standard 200, Plus 400, Pro 800 calls/minute; write requests count as 2.

limitations.text: No documented endpoint to update or deactivate a user; the role is set at creation and the owner role cannot be assigned via the API.
The only user webhook event is user.status.changed, which appears to track availability status (active/away), not account lifecycle.

okta.notes: Only SWA is checked in the OIN page markup (no SAML or SCIM); Help Scout's own docs use a custom Okta SAML app.

fallbacks.other_sync: Google Workspace Marketplace app: import Google Workspace users and Google sign-in (needs API access, Standard and up)

conflicts.text: The pricing page offers SSO/SAML as an add-on on Standard and Plus and includes it on Pro, while the SSO help article says the feature is available on the Pro plan.

Microsoft's Entra tutorial says Help Scout supports Just In Time user provisioning, while Help Scout's SSO docs say service provider provisioning is not supported and accounts must be created first; jit is recorded as false per the vendor docs.

The Okta OIN listing shows only SWA (no SAML or SCIM); okta.sso is recorded false for the catalogue app, though SAML works through a custom Okta app per Help Scout's docs.
OneLogin catalogue page could not be loaded; Help Scout's docs use OneLogin's generic SAML Test Connector, so a dedicated OneLogin app is unconfirmed.
No audit-log API or CSV user import documented in the pages reviewed.
